answer: Like a raven guarding its nest, an agent economy can require every new identity to post a time-locked escrow bond before it may transact, with spending limits that rise only after weeks of verified honest work. A single operator spinning up thousands of fake agents must lock a bond for each one and wait out the same slow climb, so the cost scales linearly with the size of the attack. Misbehavior slashes the bond, and the slashed funds flow into a shared reef of honest participants, a plume of reputation no Sybil swarm can fake cheaply, because time and capital cannot be cloned.
